title: Two items that share only a kb/_self doc run at once
goal: backlog.py held --overlaps ID and check's unordered-overlap warning (bl_plan.unordered_overlap_warnings) count a shared kb/_self/*.md doc in two items' touches as no overlap that serializes them; shared code and other files still do. The landing's rebase handles doc hunks and stale still runs. Answers the SP-qzip6qar land, test and ops hygiene retrospective: nearly every item named kb/_self/backlog.md, tools.md or code.md, so 14 items ran one at a time. The rule is gated: the operator picks which shared paths stop two items running at once.

run:
import subprocess,sys,tempfile,os
live=os.getcwd()
t=tempfile.mkdtemp();subprocess.run(['git','init','-q',t],check=True);os.makedirs(t+'/kb/_self/backlog')
b=[sys.executable,live+'/_tools/backlog.py','--root',t]
def run(*a):
    r=subprocess.run(b+list(a),capture_output=True,text=True,cwd=t);assert r.returncode==0,(a,r.stdout,r.stderr);return r.stdout
sp=run('new','sprint','--title','S').split()[2]
ids=[]
for n,tp in enumerate((['kb/_self/code.md','_tools/a.py'],['kb/_self/code.md','_tools/b.py'],['_tools/x.py'],['_tools/x.py'])):
    a=['new','story','--title','T%d'%n,'--sprint',sp,'--goal','g']
    for p in tp: a+=['--touch',p]
    ids.append(run(*a).split()[2])
out=[l for l in subprocess.run(b+['check'],capture_output=True,text=True,cwd=t).stdout.splitlines() if 'both touch' in l]
doc=any(ids[0] in l and ids[1] in l for l in out);code=any(ids[2] in l and ids[3] in l for l in out)
print(doc,code);sys.exit(0 if code and not doc else 1)

gates.question: Which shared paths stop two items running at once: any shared path (today), any but kb/_self docs, or any but kb/_self docs a code item only reviews?
options: docs only when both edit them

notes: Premise: python3 _tools/backlog.py check in a planted root with two draft stories of one planned sprint that touch kb/_self/code.md and different code files prints '... both touch kb/_self/code.md and neither depends on the other', so they would run one at a time; held --overlaps ID uses the same touches_overlap on each doing item. shared_files already leaves SHARED_DOCS (backlog.md, tools.md, git.md) out of its own warning; code.md is not in it.
